title: A Touch Is Not a Fusion

scenes.tts: Two fine nerve branches meet. Do they touch, or do they fuse? A stain that marks every cell body shows a crowd of round cell bodies. The thin branches stay almost invisible. Golgi's black reaction fills a few neurons completely, and most cells stay pale. So a single branch can be followed all the way. But where it meets another cell, the picture gives no clear answer.
scenes.visual: Two branches (blue, yellow) draw in toward each other; touch and fuse mini-icons appear; stain label; a question mark at the junction.
scenes.narration: Two fine nerve branches meet. Do they touch, or do they fuse? A stain that marks every cell body shows a crowd of round cell bodies. The thin branches stay almost invisible. Golgi's black reaction fills a few neurons completely, and most cells stay pale. So a single branch can be followed all the way. But where it meets another cell, the picture gives no clear answer.

scenes.tts: Both camps looked at similar preparations. The light microscope cannot separate two points closer than about 0.2 micrometers. Two branches that touch fall inside that limit. Branches that only pass close at different depths in a thick section look the same. So the image cannot tell contact from fusion.

scenes.visual: A red resolution disc covers the junction; two dots inside merge to one; a side view of a thick section shows branches at different depths that project onto each other.
scenes.narration: Both camps looked at similar preparations. The light microscope cannot separate two points closer than about 0.2 micrometers. Two branches that touch fall inside that limit. Branches that only pass close at different depths in a thick section look the same. So the image cannot tell contact from fusion.

scenes.tts: Each camp filled the blind spot with what its theory predicted. Golgi saw no visible join, and thought the joins were too fine to see. His network was made of axon branches. Cajal found axon branches that end close to other cells without joining them. For Cajal, those free endings were the evidence. Under the neuron theory, signals pass between cells at points of contact.
scenes.visual: The same blurred junction twice: Golgi panel fills the blind spot with a join, Cajal panel with a gap.

Cajal found axon branches that end close to other cells without joining them. For Cajal, those free endings were the evidence. Under the neuron theory, signals pass between cells at points of contact.

scenes.tts: The direct test needed a finer instrument. In the nineteen fifties, researchers used the electron microscope on synapses. At a chemical synapse, the membranes of two cells stay separate across a narrow cleft. Small vesicles crowd in the terminal. The cleft is 10 to 20 nanometers wide. That is about ten times smaller than the light microscope can resolve.

scenes.visual: Zoom into the junction: two membranes with a cleft, vesicles in the left terminal, a scale comparison of a long red limit bar and a short green cleft bar.
scenes.narration: The direct test needed a finer instrument. In the 1950s, researchers used the electron microscope on synapses. At a chemical synapse, the membranes of two cells stay separate across a narrow cleft. Small vesicles crowd in the terminal. The cleft is 10 to 20 nanometers wide. That is about ten times smaller than the light microscope can resolve.

scenes.tts: There is one real exception. Gap junctions join some neurons, especially in development. At an electrical synapse, channels cross from one cell's membrane to the next. Ions and small molecules pass straight through. Even so, each neuron keeps its own membrane. The channels pass only molecules up to roughly one kilodalton, and they can close. So the neurons are coupled, but they are not one cell.
scenes.visual: Channels bridge the two membranes; small teal dots pass through, a large grey dot is blocked; channels close; the membranes stay.
scenes.narration: There is one real exception. Gap junctions join some neurons, especially in development. At an electrical synapse, channels cross from one cell's membrane to the next. Ions and small molecules pass straight through. Even so, each neuron keeps its own membrane. The channels pass only molecules up to roughly one kilodalton, and they can close. So the neurons are coupled, but they are not one cell.

scenes.tts: So Golgi's network, in the sense he meant it, does not exist. What exists is coupling through regulated pores between separate cells. Keep this rule. Each neuron keeps its own membrane, however closely it touches.
scenes.visual: The blind-spot disc fades and the two cells show their own green membrane outlines, with a gap-junction link between them.
